addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- sonnet-worker: Cheaper, faster Sonnet-backed worker for well-scoped, mechanical, or high-volume subtasks where Opus-level reasoning isn't needed. Delegate to it when the work is clearly specified and the main agent only needs the result back to verify. Good for: applying a defined set of edits across many files, running a known pipeline/script and reporting output, broad codebase/file searches, bulk text rewrites or formatting, repetitive renames, gathering facts from many files. NOT for: ambiguous specs, tricky debugging, architecture decisions, or anything where the approach itself is the hard part — keep those on the main Opus agent. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- brand-voice-enforcement: This skill applies brand guidelines to content creation. It should be used when the user asks to "write an email", "draft a proposal", "create a pitch deck", "write a LinkedIn post", "draft a presentation", "write a Slack message", "draft sales content", or any content creation request where brand voice should be applied. Also triggers on "on-brand", "brand voice", "enforce voice", "apply brand guidelines", "brand-aligned content", "write in our voice", "use our brand tone", "make this sound like us", "rewrite this in our tone", or "this doesn't sound on-brand". Not for generating guidelines from scratch (use guideline-generation) or discovering brand materials (use discover-brand).
- build-pipeline: Use to run a non-trivial feature, bug fix, behavior change, refactor, docs-only change, or feature removal through the full spec-to-ship pipeline. Use it as well to set a project up on live-spec, where it reads the tree, picks the setup walk, and runs it. Spoken: attach live-spec to this project, adopt or install live-spec here, onboard this codebase onto live-spec, found a new project on live-spec, update live-spec here. A tiny reversible edit and pure research stay outside the pipeline.
- cold-email: Write B2B cold emails and follow-up sequences that get replies. Use when the user wants to write cold outreach emails, prospecting emails, cold email campaigns, sales development emails, or SDR emails. Also use when the user mentions "cold outreach," "prospecting email," "outbound email," "email to leads," "reach out to prospects," "sales email," "follow-up email sequence," "nobody's replying to my emails," or "how do I write a cold email." Covers subject lines, opening lines, body copy, CTAs, personalization, and multi-touch follow-up sequences. For warm/lifecycle email sequences, see emails. For sales collateral beyond emails, see sales-enablement.
- communicator: Use to show work to a human and ask for a decision, when a landing or milestone is REPORTED, to answer "did we do X", to show what the product does, or to raise a problem that needs their word. NOT a reason to LOAD it: a passing mid-work narration line, an internal working note, or a plain factual answer — those just get said.
- community-marketing: Build and leverage online communities to drive product growth and brand loyalty. Use when the user wants to create a community strategy, grow a Discord or Slack community, manage a forum or subreddit, build brand advocates, increase word-of-mouth, drive community-led growth, engage users post-signup, or turn customers into evangelists. Trigger phrases: "build a community," "community strategy," "Discord community," "Slack community," "community-led growth," "brand advocates," "user community," "forum strategy," "community engagement," "grow our community," "ambassador program," "community flywheel."
- copy-editing: When the user wants to edit, review, or improve existing marketing copy, or refresh outdated content. Also use when the user mentions 'edit this copy,' 'review my copy,' 'copy feedback,' 'proofread,' 'polish this,' 'make this better,' 'copy sweep,' 'tighten this up,' 'this reads awkwardly,' 'clean up this text,' 'too wordy,' 'sharpen the messaging,' 'refresh this content,' 'update this page,' 'this content is outdated,' or 'content audit.' Use this when the user already has copy and wants it improved or refreshed rather than rewritten from scratch. For writing new copy, see copywriting.
- copywriting: When the user wants to write, rewrite, or improve marketing copy for any page — including homepage, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, about pages, or product pages. Also use when the user says "write copy for," "improve this copy," "rewrite this page," "marketing copy," "headline help," "CTA copy," "value proposition," "tagline," "subheadline," "hero section copy," "above the fold," "this copy is weak," "make this more compelling," or "help me describe my product." Use this whenever someone is working on website text that needs to persuade or convert. For email copy, see emails. For popup copy, see popups. For editing existing copy, see copy-editing. For the offer underneath the copy (bonuses, guarantees, value framing), see offers.
- customer-research: When the user wants to conduct, analyze, or synthesize customer research. Use when the user mentions "customer research," "ICP research," "talk to customers," "analyze transcripts," "customer interviews," "survey analysis," "support ticket analysis," "voice of customer," "VOC," "build personas," "customer personas," "jobs to be done," "JTBD," "what do customers say," "what are customers struggling with," "Reddit mining," "G2 reviews," "review mining," "digital watering holes," "community research," "forum research," "competitor reviews," "customer sentiment," or "find out why customers churn/convert/buy." Use for both analyzing existing research assets AND gathering new research from online sources. For writing copy informed by research, see copywriting. For acting on research to improve pages, see cro.
- design-reviewer: Use after a spec is proven to check whether similar features behave consistently and flag ungrouped same-kind items the spec missed. It holds no landing; every finding is a recommendation or a question.
- directory-submissions: When the user wants to submit their product to startup, SaaS, AI, agent, MCP, no-code, or review directories for backlinks, domain rating, and discovery. Also use when the user mentions "directory submissions," "submit to directories," "backlinks from directories," "list my product," "submit to Product Hunt," "BetaList," "TAAFT," "Futurepedia," "G2 listing," "Capterra listing," "AlternativeTo," "SaaSHub," "AI directories," "MCP registry," "agent directory," "dofollow backlinks," "launch directories," or "directory tracker." Use this whenever someone is planning the directory layer of a product launch or an ongoing backlink campaign. For the broader launch moment, see launch. For programmatic SEO pages that should live behind these backlinks, see programmatic-seo. For AI citation optimization, see ai-seo.
- discover-brand: This skill orchestrates autonomous discovery of brand materials across enterprise platforms (Notion, Confluence, Google Drive, Box, SharePoint, Figma, Gong, Granola, Slack). It should be used when the user asks to "discover brand materials", "find brand documents", "search for brand guidelines", "audit brand content", "what brand materials do we have", "find our style guide", "where are our brand docs", "do we have a style guide", "discover brand voice", "brand content audit", or "find brand assets".
- feedback-collector: Use, only if enabled, when the user shows a rare, strong reaction (delight or frustration) to offer drafting a private note to the pack's authors. Consent is asked every time, and the skill never sends the note — delivery is the human's own step.
- feedback-intake: Use whenever feedback arrives — a comment, answer, file, or reaction from a person, a file appearing in inbox/ (whoever put it there, person or agent), an inbox sweep, or an append to the feedback ledger FEEDBACK.md — and route it to where it belongs.
- guideline-generation: This skill generates, creates, or builds brand voice guidelines from source materials. It should be used when the user asks to "generate brand guidelines", "create a style guide", "extract brand voice", "create guidelines from calls", "consolidate brand materials", "analyze my sales calls for brand voice", "build a brand playbook from documents", "synthesize a voice and tone guide", or uploads brand documents, transcripts, or meeting recordings for brand analysis. Also triggers when the user has a discovery report and wants to convert it into actionable guidelines.
- launch: When the user wants to plan a product launch, feature announcement, or release strategy. Also use when the user mentions 'launch,' 'Product Hunt,' 'feature release,' 'announcement,' 'go-to-market,' 'beta launch,' 'early access,' 'waitlist,' 'product update,' 'how do I launch this,' 'launch checklist,' 'GTM plan,' or 'we're about to ship.' Use this whenever someone is preparing to release something publicly. For ongoing marketing after launch, see marketing-ideas. For the offer being launched (bonuses, guarantees, scarcity, naming), see offers.
- live-spec-base: Load before using any live-spec pack skill (spec-author, product-prover, design-reviewer, build-pipeline, test-author, communicator, feedback-intake, feedback-collector, text-audit, publish), before briefing a worker that will write files, or to resolve shared rules and settings. It is the one home for the shared rules — thirty-four rules in the body — and for the settings ladder.
- marketing-psychology: When the user wants to apply psychological principles, mental models, or behavioral science to marketing. Also use when the user mentions 'psychology,' 'mental models,' 'cognitive bias,' 'persuasion,' 'behavioral science,' 'why people buy,' 'decision-making,' 'consumer behavior,' 'anchoring,' 'social proof,' 'scarcity,' 'loss aversion,' 'framing,' or 'nudge.' Use this whenever someone wants to understand or leverage how people think and make decisions in a marketing context. For applying psychology to specific pages, see cro; for pricing tactics, see pricing; for copy framing, see copywriting.
- ogilvy: Apply David Ogilvy's advertising principles when writing or reviewing copy, headlines, product descriptions, landing pages, ads, emails, or any persuasive text. Use when the goal is copy that sells, not copy that wins awards. Covers positioning, headlines, promises, brand voice, long-form copy, and visual logic. Source: How to Create Advertising That Sells (1972) + Ogilvy on Advertising.
- product-marketing: When the user wants to create or update their product marketing context document. Also use when the user mentions 'product context,' 'marketing context,' 'set up context,' 'positioning,' 'who is my target audience,' 'describe my product,' 'ICP,' 'ideal customer profile,' or wants to avoid repeating foundational information across marketing tasks. Use this at the start of any new project before using other marketing skills — it creates `.agents/product-marketing.md` that all other skills reference for product, audience, and positioning context.
- product-prover: Structured senior-architect review of product documents: PRDs, feature specs, HLDs, LLDs, design proposals, and architecture documents. It reviews them with formal-verification thinking, covering entities, states, transitions, invariants, safety, liveness, atomicity, and composition. Use this skill whenever the user asks to review, critique, stress-test, lint, or find gaps in a spec or design document. It fires as well when they ask "is this spec ready / what did I miss / poke holes in this". It fires on an uploaded product document with a request for feedback, and on the words "Product Prover". A request for feedback counts even where the word "review" goes unsaid. It reads documents, so code and diffs route elsewhere. It finds holes in what a document claims, and the test suite proves what the artifact does. It answers "does the spec hold together as written?"
- public-relations: When the user wants help with public relations, earned media, press coverage, journalist outreach, or media strategy (not pull requests). Also use when the user mentions 'PR,' 'public relations,' 'press,' 'press release,' 'press coverage,' 'media outreach,' 'pitch a journalist,' 'get featured,' 'media list,' 'media kit,' 'press kit,' 'newsjacking,' 'news hijack,' 'HARO,' 'Qwoted,' 'Featured,' 'Help A Reporter,' 'reporter request,' 'tech press,' 'TechCrunch,' 'earned media,' 'thought leadership placement,' 'op-ed,' 'guest article,' 'press contacts,' or 'how do I get press.' Use this for earned media work — finding journalists, pitching stories, newsjacking, and responding to press requests. For startup/SaaS/AI directory submissions, see directory-submissions. For product launches, see launch. For social-media engagement, see social. For cold-email outreach to prospects, see cold-email.
- publish: Use before work leaves the machine publicly — a public repo, README push, release, or shared skill — to check it meets publish quality. It finishes before the human's own publish decision and only prepares it.
- restore-readability: Rewrite one auto-loaded document into plain readable language while keeping every rule and the document's structure (rule numbers, anchors, file paths, thresholds). Runs a worker pipeline with four verification gates and a human replacement gate. One document per iteration.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- social: When the user wants help creating, scheduling, or optimizing social media content for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, or other platforms, or wants to do social listening and engagement triage. Also use when the user mentions 'LinkedIn post,' 'Twitter thread,' 'social media,' 'content calendar,' 'social scheduling,' 'engagement,' 'viral content,' 'what should I post,' 'repurpose this content,' 'tweet ideas,' 'LinkedIn carousel,' 'social media strategy,' 'grow my following,' 'TikTok video,' 'Reels,' 'Shorts,' 'video script,' 'video hook,' 'short-form video,' 'create a reel,' 'social listening,' 'brand mentions,' 'competitor monitoring,' 'top posts to comment on,' or 'find people asking for.' Use this for social media content creation, repurposing, scheduling, short-form video scripting, and social listening. For broader content strategy, see content-strategy. For paid ads, see ad-creative. For earned media, see public-relations.
- spec-author: Use to start a new product spec, add a feature to an existing spec, or keep a spec in sync with behavior changes. Setting a project up on live-spec comes earlier, at build-pipeline's setup entry. Documenting already-built code after the fact and a prototype sketch that carries no spec stay outside it.
- stop-slop: Remove AI writing patterns from prose. Use when drafting, editing, or reviewing text to eliminate predictable AI tells and produce more human-like writing.
- test-author: Use to derive a test matrix and write tests from a proven spec and architecture. Not a substitute for reviewing the spec itself.
- text-audit: Use to check any human-facing text — README, spec, copy, article — for places a first-time reader stops, then repair them.
- track-coach: Full-stack compositional coach for music producers. Runs everything by default: audio arc analysis, Demucs stem separation, frequency masking, per-stem rhythm + separation-quality, drum-hit breakdown (kick/snare/hat), note transcription, AND Ableton .als parsing (tracks, MIDI, AUDIO clips, automation envelopes, locators). Builds one offline HTML widget with a synced multi-stem PLAYER (play/seek/mute/solo, playhead linked to every chart), the real project arrangement on the timeline, an automation "intention vs result" layer, and a Demucs-stem ↔ real-track map. Gives concrete, specific diagnostics — not generic numbers, but "bass masks mid in 250–500 Hz during bars 8–24" and "Cutoff automation ends at 2:45 but brightness keeps rising to 3:10".
ALWAYS USE THIS SKILL when the user mentions: a track, a mix, an arrangement, an .als file, "why does it sound stuck/raw/flat/cloudy", "compare versions", "check the arc", "analyse my project", "what's happening in my track" — even casually, even without the word "analyse". Grab the audio file AND the .als if available. Run everything. Don't ask permission to run Deep mode — just do it and narrate while Demucs runs.
Supports mp3 / wav / m4a / aiff / flac + Ableton .als. macOS only (v1).
- tc: Track Coach — full deep analysis (stems, player, evidence). Opens calm by default.
- tc-quick: Track Coach — quick calm read (fast & cheap, no stems). Upgradeable to full later.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Session rules (live-spec), short form. Seven laws follow. Act on them as they stand. Full texts: ~/.claude/live-spec/profile.md and ~/.claude/skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md. Where two rules answer one case differently, name the clash to the human as a policy question.
1. Answer first (live-spec): open every reply with the outcome; detail follows below it, and going longer than that waits for the human to ask. Home: the personal profile, key language.answer-first.
2. Plain words and narration (live-spec): use plain product words with the human. Internal codes and project-coined metaphors may only trail in parentheses at the end of a line. Check a candidate word against guardrails/spec-coinages.json before writing it and replace any word that list holds; replace any other word an outside reader, never taught this project's private vocabulary, would read as jargon. Narrate while working: write a line whenever a pipeline step passes, a discovery changes the plan, or the work turns, naming which wish is in hand and which pipeline step it stands at. A wish is one request the human voiced, held as a row in the queue ROADMAP.md. A finished step gets a digest of two or three sentences; and after ~10 minutes with no line, write one naming what is still running. Home: base rule 2 (SPEC INV-28), and the narration law (SPEC INV-35).
3. The human's own words (live-spec): in chat use the standard industry word in the chat language; never render pack-internal English terms word for word. Before showing an artifact — a page rendered from a document, a mockup, a decision page, or a report page, in any language — run python3 scripts/preshow-register-lint.py <path> from the project root; a non-zero exit blocks the showing. Home: the personal profile, key language.no-calques, and the register-lint law (SPEC INV-83).
4. Say what a thing is (live-spec): name each thing by its own positive sentence. The contrast frame, which puts a positive claim and a rejected alternative in one sentence ("X, not Y"), is banned in every text this session writes: chat, docs, artifacts, product copy, and worker briefs. A plain prohibition standing on its own stays lawful. Home: the personal profile, key language.no-scissors.
5. Routing (live-spec): the orchestrator seat — this session — plans, briefs, and accepts; workers execute. A unit carrying a decision or a design choice goes to opus; a multi-step mechanical unit to sonnet; a single step to haiku. Those three lines set the cheapest sufficient tier, and how much text or how many files a unit touches never moves a unit to another tier. Workers locate their own anchors, meaning the files and lines their task needs. A long read that must end in a verdict or a decision from this session stays here; a read done only to understand is dispatched to a reader worker, and this session reads the summary that worker returns. Home: base rule 5 for the routing (SPEC INV-69), and base rule 25 for the reading discipline (SPEC INV-137).
6. Deferral re-test (live-spec): before parking an item for the human or opening an AskUserQuestion, re-test it by derivability at that moment — does a written source already answer it: a base rule, PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, an approved prototype, or a past decision? If one does, the item is this session's: act on it, cite the source, and remove the marker. Park only what needs their taste, a policy call, an act that cannot be undone, or a real device, and name which one. An act cannot be undone when the project cannot return to the state before it without losing something: spending money, deleting data, a send that cannot be recalled. A push to the project's own repository reverts, so it stays with this session. A marker or a question that cannot name one of the four is itself the finding, and the item defaults to this session. Home: base rule 29 (SPEC INV-152), with the mechanical check guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py.
7. Root every act (live-spec, his word 2026-08-07 00:42 and 00:46, urgent): every work block and every report line opens by naming its root — his request with its date, a standing instruction he gave, or a reason stated plainly enough for him to judge. A root citing only machinery (an alarm, a gate, a scheduled reminder) is not a root: name the instruction of his that the machinery carries. Work whose root cannot be named does not start; a report line whose root is missing is a defect. Home: the grounded-work wish, ROADMAP row 569.

Without `12f6f8b`, the installer test would have red inside that copy and taken gate b down **in CI**. That commit is not local convenience.
- **Protected-path history** clean over all 24 commits of `acf0e3c..HEAD`: `git log --name-only --format= acf0e3c..HEAD | sort -u | grep -E "PROBLEMS|culling-plan|PROGRESS"` → no match; nothing under `.live-spec/` changed at all. Linear, no merges, no rewritten history, no upstream tracking ref → never pushed.
- **Notes, none blocking:** (N1) the fence keys on `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` where the surrounding convention keys on `LIVE_SPEC_SCRATCH`; it fails safe in the direction that matters (false-red, never false-green) — kept deliberately, since the cause is the missing index, not scratch-ness. (N3) `fell: PRODUCT_SPEC.md — recorded 1863, measured 1862` is pre-existing on `cd6ef7b`, informational, checker exits 0.

**Still running:** the one clone-present CI-equivalent full suite (pinned canon `94d3645` installed into the gitignored `skills/product-prover/`). Merge-readiness verdict follows it, not before.

---

**Full suite #1, clone-present (pinned canon `94d3645`), 23m 56s: 4 failed, 2,548 passed.** Against the candidate's own final run (7 failed, 2,544 passed) the gate-f pair and `landing-next-steps` are closed and nothing new appears in the outer set.   finding from this wave in any tree.
- **blocker** none for the branch. Merging is the owner's act and four decisions below precede a push.
- **next action** merge as one unit `acf0e3c..cd6ef7b`; then a push owes its own record over the
  real push range.

### Now — mandatory-context map · `mandatory-load-manifest.md`
- **state** measured; the uncertainties are named, not smoothed.
- **owner** Lane B.
- **proof** always-load floor **6,277 bytes / 1 file + 2 hook injections** — `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
  (1,621 B) and the stdout of `clock-hook.sh` (172 B) and `chat-law-hook.sh` (4,484 B), which fire
  on **every prompt**, not just the first. Per scenario: plain chat 6,277 B · local code change
  135,033 B · cross-cutting feature 198,066 B · document audit 101,800 B · skill change 135,033 B.
  Byte counts are `wc -c` on real paths; no token estimate was made.
- **blocker** **no skill body is proven to load at startup.** No loader, registry or manifest was
  found; discovery is the host's own description-matching. So the cost is per-route, not at boot.
- **next action** the reducible mass is `live-spec-base` (64,728 B) + `build-pipeline` (64,028 B),
  paid on every code change. Split the base's settings ladder out first — see R2.5 below.

### Now — skill-package map · `logical-skill-map.md`
- **state** all eleven packages mapped as whole packages (SKILL.md, README, references, scripts,
  templates, examples, tests/evals, install/sync wiring). 501,137 shipped bytes.
- **owner** Lane C, eleven independent read-only workers.
- **proof** per-package surfaces with exact bytes, triggers, dependencies, load tier, blockers.
- **blocker — and this is the wave's largest single finding.** Both gates you made mandatory are
  unmet across the whole pack: **no README in the pack has ever been cold-read** (all ~28 records
  in `docs/language-reads/` read the text-audit skill itself), and **no package has an eval result
  produced against the body it ships today** — nine stale, one bare-arm only, one never evaluated,
  one exempt by a written rule. `text-audit`, the route that judges everyone else, has run 16
  self-audits and **never once reached its own closing criterion of two consecutive clean rounds**.
- **next action** produce the two missing proofs for exactly ONE package and measure what it costs.

### Now — readability baseline · `readability-baseline.md`
- **state** five canonical document types measured.
- **owner** Lane D.
- **proof** `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` 703,511 B / 8,225 lines / 1,863 criteria · `ROADMAP.md` 300,344 B
  over 281 lines (~1,069 B/line, ~9× denser than the rest) · `ARCHITECTURE.md` 107,380 B and
  **named in no byte bound at all** · `MIGRATION.md` classified as a record, so never measured,
  though it is an executed operating guide · skills 5,861 B → 64,348 B.
- **blocker** the "comprehension gate" the format documents is implemented by **no script**;
  `criterion-readability.json` is hardcoded to govern `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` alone. The one arm that
  does measure prose admits its own debt: 469 of 1,461 criteria are frozen over the 35-word cap.
- **next action** the single criterion that is measurable today and false today:
  `python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py` exits 0 on the live tree.

### Next — the R2 vertical slice: Parameter and Policy Ownership
- **state** inventory done, `defaults-and-thresholds.md`: ~78 parameters, and **~38 are unowned
  AI-invented candidates** — the largest bucket by far. 10 owner-confirmed, ~20 evidence-backed,
  4 inherited-compatibility, 5 stale.
- **owner** you. None of these numbers may be presented as your decision until you have made it.
- **proof** each row carries its source, the commit that introduced it, and whether that commit
  gave a reason. The five that matter most:
  1. `check-worker-restore.py DEFAULT_SINCE_HOURS = 24.0` — the destructive-git scan window;
     ROADMAP row 527 already says your word is owed here.
  2. `gate_common.py MAX_WAIVER_DAYS = 30` — how long a lint exemption stands before CI hard-fails.
  3. `spec-redundancy-precheck.py JAC=0.60 / CON=0.85 / MIN_TOKENS=6` — defines "redundant" across
     the whole spec, hand-duplicated into `language-rules.json` with no drift check.
  4. `check-runaway-child.py CPU_THRESHOLD=50.0%` and `reap_owned_group.py IDLE_THRESHOLD=120.0s`
     — they auto-terminate worker processes, both claim to be host-settable, and **no override
     mechanism exists**. This wave met them: a baseline suite was SIGKILLed mid-run.
  5. `progress-baseline.json` estimate inputs (`rounds_expected=5`, `working_hours_per_day=6`,
     `parallel_lanes=4`) — they feed every projection a reader sees, and the file itself calls
     `rounds_expected` "the weakest input here".
- **blocker** the candidate should land first, so the tree stops moving under the registry.
- **next action** rule on those five; the survivors get a home the route scheduler can read.

### Later
**R2.3 human docs** — the five types, one measurable criterion each; `ARCHITECTURE.md` gets a
declared bound, `MIGRATION.md` stops being classified as a record. **R2.5 logical skills** —
on-demand without extraction, in the order the evidence gives: the base's settings ladder, then
the two 64 KB bodies. **Physical extraction** — blocked on evidence, not machinery (below).
**Events, board, onboarding, migration** — untouched by this wave, by charter.

---

## Lane A — the candidate, in full

### Why a new branch existed at all
The previous candidate let `docs/PROGRESS.md` enter commit `b8d53f2` and removed it in `5ea60dd`.
A clean final tree is not enough for a protected file — the path must appear in **no commit**.
The ten approved commits were replayed onto `acf0e3c`, with `b8d53f2` replayed **minus its
protected-file hunk**: base bytes written back, only the two test paths staged, no discarding git
command (INV-298/299). `git diff <new> 5ea60dd` returned exactly one file, the old prover record —
so the new branch is provably the old candidate minus the protected-file episode.

### The four fresh-review findings, each proven red first
| # | finding | commit | red → green |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | tracked assertions skipped when the clone is absent | `057c87b` | mutate a TRACKED needle, bare checkout: before `1 passed, 3 SKIPPED`; after `1 FAILED, 4 passed, 3 skipped` naming `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` |
| 2 | whitespace flattening weakened locality on tracked docs | `9e46503` | wrap two TRACKED needles across a line break: before `10 passed, 5 skipped`; after `2 FAILED` in both modules |
| 3 | CI proved nothing of the external canon | `f100c73` | installer removed → `2 failed`; pin loosened to a tag → `1 failed`; installer after the suite → `1 failed`; unmutated `15 passed` |
| 3b | the fence that model requires | `5e214b2` | unfenced+clone `3 FAILED`; unfenced+bare `1 FAILED`; fenced `13 passed` in **both** environments |

Every mutation was made on a disposable copy or in a scratch tree outside the repository, and
every restore was a byte write with the hash verified — never `git checkout --`, `git restore`,
`git stash`, `git reset`, `git rebase` or `git clean`, in any tree.

### The CI authority model — chosen, implemented, and its cost stated
**CI installs the external canon**, pinned to commit `94d3645…` and verified with
`--expect-commit`. Re-homing every canon assertion onto tracked evidence was rejected: it would
have deleted proof rather than moved it. `v1.3.0` was rejected as the pin because
`tests/test_class_hunt.py` reads the canon's `README.md`, which differs between that tag and the
state the pack's needles were written against — a pin must name what is actually proven.

**The trade, stated rather than hidden:** the gates job now depends on a third-party repository
being reachable, and a network failure there reds CI. That is an honest failure. The previous
shape was a dishonest green.

### What the independent reviewer refused, and what it cost
An adversarial reviewer briefed to refuse returned **REFUSE** with three blocking findings — all
three consequences of choosing to install the canon, and all three closed:

1. **`ARCHITECTURE.md` pinned line numbers inside the external repository.** With no clone, gate g
   read "pinned file missing" and walked past. Install the canon and all three read as *drifted* —
   the pack red in CI for an edit made in a repository it cannot fix. Closed by `35f3977`: the pins
   moved onto the tracked adapter, and the rule is asserted as a class — no `ARCHITECTURE.md` pin
   may point into any external skill root, with the roster read from tracked `requires:` lines.
   Gate g: **OK, 209 pins, in both environments**; FAILED at base.
2. **The published skills line count became unsatisfiable** (5,528 bare vs 6,365 with the canon —
   no single number can be right in both). Closed by `db6c0d9`: the shared pattern expander fences
   external skills, block rebuilt to 5,528/4,290. Gate ad: **OK in both environments**; red at base.
3. **The installer-ordering assertion read the whole workflow file**, so a step in the other job
   satisfied it while `gates` installed nothing. Closed by `1ebc6e8`: reader scoped to the `gates`
   job, scope pinned both ways.

A fourth, non-blocking: a test claiming to compare the pin against the adapter floor asserted only
that a digit capture held digits — it could not fail. Split into a tracked half and a real
comparison.

One **out-of-packet one-liner, named as such**: `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:634 (ladder)` was
drifted six lines from its heading at `:628`, at the base too. It was the only thing left keeping
gate g red, so the number was corrected and nothing else.

### What the first complete suite caught, and nothing else could
Renaming the restructure-merge tests orphaned `TEST_MATRIX.md` row M-253, which still named a
function that no longer exists. Focused runs cannot see this; the whole-suite matrix check can.
Closed by `f09a876`.

### The four complete suites
Strictly one at a time on one machine, each a whole `python3 -m pytest -q --durations=25`.

| run | result | wall |
|---|---|---|
| **final, tracked-only** (no clone) | **7 failed, 2,491 passed, 54 skipped** | 16m 49s |
| **final, clone-present** (what CI now carries) | **7 failed, 2,544 passed, 1 skipped** | 16m 03s |
| baseline `acf0e3c`, tracked-only | 73 failed, 2,448 passed, 1 skipped | 15m 42s |
| baseline `acf0e3c`, clone-present | 68 failed, 2,453 passed, 1 skipped | 16m 08s |

**Complete node-id sets compared, not samples. Introduced: none, in either environment** —
`comm -23 final baseline` is empty both ways. Closed: **66** tracked-only, **61** clone-present.

Two properties worth naming, because they are what the range was for:
- the final failure set is the **same seven node ids in both environments** — the candidate no
  longer behaves differently depending on whether the reader ran the installer;
- the 54 skips of the tracked-only run become 53 further passes with the canon present
  (2,491 + 53 = 2,544). Every skip is accounted for rather than silent.

**The seven that remain, all present in both baseline sets:** two real-`~/.claude` config-health
(environmental), gate f's missing proof function `test_broken_skill_fails` plus its cascade, gate b
(which runs the whole suite inside itself and reds while anything above reds — inner run
`6 failed, 2,533 passed`), `test_landing_next_steps` whose message names `acf0e3c1` *itself* as the
offending landing, and worker-restore reading this machine's transcripts.

**One red the candidate closes rather than leaves:** `TestGateA_ProverRecord::test_real_repo_passes`
fails at both baselines and passes on both final runs.

**Cost the CI model adds:** the pinned installer step, 1.6s. The suite's own shape dominates
instead — gate b 218.5s, then `TestGateG_PinDrift` and `TestCIMirror` at 39–91s each.

### The prover decision, on the cited law
**No FULL pass is owed and none was run.** The trigger is written for a MINOR bump
(`skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md:49`; `references/minor-bump-gate.md:1`). Of the documents a
review reads, this range touches `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` by exactly one line — the H1 version banner —
and one `**pins**` block of `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**The law is genuinely silent on whether a MAJOR bump owes a FULL pass, and this wave left it
silent** rather than picking the reading that suited the pass. That is owner decision 1.

A record is committed: `docs/prover/2026-08-14-candidate-repair.md`, a non-push pass record — the
form `docs/prover/README.md` provides for. It names no prover version because none ran. It carries
**no `PUSH-REVIEW` marker**: an honest push record must name `be4e4f0..HEAD`, 21 commits, and this
pass read 20 of them (`PRODUCT_SPEC.md:3235` — a record naming another range covers nothing). Gate
a's freshness arm is now green on the branch and red at base; its push arm still refuses, correctly.

### Merge order and the remaining owner action
1. **Merge the candidate as one unit, `acf0e3c..cd6ef7b`.** Its later commits depend on its earlier
   ones; do not merge it packet by packet.
2. `night/2026-08-13-ck2-neutral` (`6915ef5`) stays unmerged pending the lane-cap ruling, unchanged
   by this wave.
3. The three earlier night branches and `night/2026-08-13-integration` are **superseded** by this
   candidate; keep or delete at your discretion, but do not merge them alongside it.
4. The emergency branch remains unreconciled; harvest-then-abandon is still the standing
   recommendation.
5. **A push owes a record over the real push range** (`be4e4f0..`), which this wave could not
   honestly write.

---

## Lanes B–F — the maps

| lane | artifact | the one thing to read |
|---|---|---|
| B | `mandatory-load-manifest.md` | the always-load floor is 6,277 B; no skill loads at startup; the installed prover is a **different generation** from the repo clone (v4.3.0 monolith, 71,781 B, no `reference/` — against v1.3.0 + a mandatory 30,863 B `stress-lenses.md`) |
| C | `logical-skill-map.md` | both mandatory gates unmet for every package; `product-prover-pack` has never been reviewed or evaluated at all |
| D | `readability-baseline.md` | the comprehension gate is implemented by no script; `ARCHITECTURE.md` has no declared bound; gate aa is red on the live tree |
| E | `runtime-surface-inventory.md` | ~40 surfaces, 29 gate letters; gate m is **red right now** (installed pre-push drifted, 6 skills drifted, `product-prover-pack` missing from `~/.claude/skills`); **no surface qualified as a retire-candidate** under the two-condition rule |
| F | `defaults-and-thresholds.md` | ~38 of ~78 parameters are unowned AI-invented candidates |

### The three north stars, source-anchored

**1. Mandatory context — bytes and files.** Floor **6,277 B / 1 file + 2 hook injections**, every
turn. Per-route: 135,033 B for a local code change, 198,066 B for a cross-cutting feature,
101,800 B for a document audit. The pack ships 501,137 B of skill packages; two skills are 35% of
it. The reduction target is per-route, not startup — nothing loads at boot.

**2. Human readability — baseline and evidence.** Five document types measured, sizes above. The
existing evidence is thinner than the machinery suggests: one prose gate governs one file, the
documented comprehension gate has no implementation, eleven READMEs have never been cold-read, and
the skill that owns cold reading has never closed its own.

**3. Behavioural proof and remaining reds.** 2,545 collected nodes. Final: **7 failed** in both
environments, identical sets, **0 introduced**, 66 closed. Gates g, ad, aa, u, ae, a and z all
green on the candidate; g, ad and a are red at the base.

### On extraction, weighed rather than assumed
`text-audit` is **not** the first extraction candidate: it is the heaviest-blocked package —
two generators write *into* its directory, gate ae's registry names two of its files by path, and
its own self-audit has never closed. By machinery alone the order is `feedback-collector` (11.9 KB,
3 files, 3 surfaces) then `design-reviewer`. **But no package is extraction-ready, and the blocker
is evidence, not machinery**: `feedback-collector`, the lightest, has no with-skill eval run at all
and carries a live version-drift red. The honest first step is not an extraction.

---

## The concrete next step, from the evidence

**R2 — do this first: the Parameter and Policy Ownership pass**, on the five numbers named above.
It is a vertical slice because it ends in a registry a machine reads, not another document, and
this wave already met one of those numbers as a live failure (a SIGKILLed suite).

**R2.3 — then, one measurable criterion per document type**, beginning with the two that are false
today and cheap to make true: give `ARCHITECTURE.md` a declared bound in `doc-bounds.json`, and
stop classifying `MIGRATION.md` as a record so the census can see it.

**R2.5 — then, on-demand without extraction, in this order**: split the settings ladder out of
`live-spec-base` (both the base worker and the map named it independently as the one clean internal
seam), then apply `communicator`'s already-proven reference-extraction pattern to the two 64 KB
bodies. No physical extraction until one package has both mandatory gates behind it.

**Not yet, and deliberately:** no skill was extracted, split, rewritten or published; no repository,
copy, installer, sync, version bump or new skill was created; no board, router, event store or
onboarding was built; nothing was merged or pushed.

# План Fable — 14.08.2026, ~10:30

Корень: запрос Александра от 14.08.2026 (написать план по трём сводкам; репозиторий не трогать, новых задач Opus не давать).

## 1. Где мы сейчас

Ночная волна собрала ветку-кандидата (`night/2026-08-14-candidate`, 20 коммитов поверх `acf0e3c`): она закрыла 66 старых падений тестов, ввела ноль новых, но в полном прогоне оставалось 7 красных, из них четыре — настоящие дефекты дерева. Утренняя миссия в отдельной рабочей копии (`green/2026-08-14-claude`) закрыла эти четыре, прошла независимую проверку («допустить, с примечаниями»), и первый полный прогон с установленным внешним каноном вскрыл ещё одну поломку внутри ворот b: их черновая копия дерева теряла `.git`, и клон канона выглядел одиннадцатым навыком с чужой версией. Это починено коммитом `4e8df4c`. Сейчас Opus гонит второй полный прогон (~16–24 мин), потому что первый изменил ту самую машинерию, которую измерял. `main` не тронут, ничего не слито и не отправлено.

## 2. Какой результат прогона меняет решение

Критерий один: в наборе падений остаются только три известные локальные проверки этой машины (две читают реальный `~/.claude`, одна — расшифровки чужих проектов), и ворота b зелёные либо красные только по той же причине, которая на CI отсутствует. Любое новое имя падения, либо красный ворот b по новой причине — вердикт «готово к слиянию» откладывается.

## 3. Если прогон зелёный

Ветка объявляется готовой к слиянию, и я готовлю короткий доклад: диапазон `acf0e3c..HEAD` сливается одним куском, а перед push нужны четыре решения Александра — честная запись за реальный диапазон push (`be4e4f0..`), политика прувера при крупном повышении версии, судьба четырёх устаревших ночных веток, судьба аварийной ветки. Автономно готовятся сводка и черновик записи; слияние и отправка ждут его слова.

## 4. Если прогон остаётся красным

Читаем имя падения. Новая поломка, вскрытая вторым прогоном, чинится тем же порядком: изолированная копия, сначала доказанный красный, точечная починка, снова полный прогон, доклад после каждого круга. Расширение известного машинного набора — находка о среде: фиксируется и выносится Александру. Правило прежнее: вердикт выдаётся только по прогону дерева в его текущем виде.

## 5. Два рубежа после целостности кандидата

**Рубеж 1 — хозяева у чисел.** Из ~78 параметров пакета ~38 придуманы ИИ и никем не утверждены. Пять главных выносятся на решение: окно сканирования опасных git-команд (24 ч), срок жизни исключений линта (30 дней), пороги «избыточности» спецификации, авто-остановка рабочих процессов (в эту волну она уже убила прогон), входы оценок сроков. Выжившие числа получают реестр, который читает машина.

**Рубеж 2 — измеримая читаемость и первый вынос.** По одному проверяемому критерию на каждый из пяти типов документов: `ARCHITECTURE.md` получает объявленный предел размера, `MIGRATION.md` перестаёт числиться архивом и попадает под перепись. Затем лестница настроек выносится из `live-spec-base` в файл, подгружаемый по запросу, с замером байтов до и после.

## 6. Что автономно, что требует Александра

Автономно: чтение прогонов, починка красных в изолированных копиях, независимые проверки, замеры контекста, черновики реестра чисел и записей, доклады. Только Александр: слияние и push; решения по пяти числам; политика прувера; судьба старых и аварийной веток; любое изменение `~/.claude`, хуков и установленных копий.

## 7. Как рубежи двигают три звезды

Утренняя миссия в отдельной рабочей копии (`green/2026-08-14-claude`) закрыла эти четыре, прошла независимую проверку («допустить, с примечаниями»), и первый полный прогон с установленным внешним каноном вскрыл ещё одну поломку внутри ворот b: их черновая копия дерева теряла `.git`, и клон канона выглядел одиннадцатым навыком с чужой версией. Это починено коммитом `4e8df4c`. Сейчас Opus гонит второй полный прогон (~16–24 мин), потому что первый изменил ту самую машинерию, которую измерял. `main` не тронут, ничего не слито и не отправлено.

## 2. Какой результат прогона меняет решение

Критерий один: в наборе падений остаются только три известные локальные проверки этой машины (две читают реальный `~/.claude`, одна — расшифровки чужих проектов), и ворота b зелёные либо красные только по той же причине, которая на CI отсутствует. Любое новое имя падения, либо красный ворот b по новой причине — статус откладывается.

## 3. Если прогон зелёный

Ветка получает статус «реализация завершена; независимая проверка отложена» — в этот малотокенный период мы никакую работу словом «готово к слиянию» не называем. Я готовлю короткий доклад с этим статусом. Слияние и push остаются решениями Александра после более поздней независимой проверки; перед push также нужны честная запись за реальный диапазон (`be4e4f0..`), политика прувера при крупном повышении версии, судьба старых ночных и аварийной веток.

## 4. Если прогон остаётся красным

Читаем имя падения. Новая поломка, вскрытая вторым прогоном, чинится тем же порядком: изолированная копия, сначала доказанный красный, точечная починка, снова полный прогон, доклад после каждого круга. Расширение известного машинного набора — находка о среде: фиксируется и выносится Александру. Итог любого круга описывается тем же осторожным статусом из пункта 3.

## 5. Два рубежа после целостности кандидата

**Рубеж 1 — первый замеренный раздел контекста.** Лестница настроек выносится из `live-spec-base` в модуль, подгружаемый по запросу; все доказательства маршрутов сохраняются; до и после выноса замеряются реальные файлы и байты маршрута локальной правки кода (сегодня 135 КБ). Опись параметров и порогов продолжается параллельно в режиме «только чтение»; пять решений хозяина чисел следующим блокером не ставятся — они ждут своего часа.

**Рубеж 2 — читаемость с живым читателем.** По одному проверяемому критерию на каждый из пяти типов документов: `ARCHITECTURE.md` получает объявленный предел размера, `MIGRATION.md` перестаёт числиться архивом и попадает под перепись. Предел по байтам сам по себе читаемости не доказывает, поэтому в рубеж входит один настоящий приёмочный тест холодного чтения (text-audit) для одной выбранной страницы, обращённой к человеку.

## 6. Что автономно, что требует Александра

Автономно: чтение прогонов, починка красных в изолированных копиях, замеры контекста до и после выноса, опись чисел в режиме чтения, черновики докладов и записей. Только Александр: слияние и push (после более поздней независимой проверки); решения по числам, когда до них дойдёт очередь; политика прувера; судьба старых и аварийной веток; любое изменение `~/.claude`, хуков и установленных копий.

## 7. Как рубежи двигают три звезды

Меньше контекста: вынос лестницы настроек — первый раздел с замером байтов до и после на живом маршруте. Читаемость: проверяемый критерий на каждый тип документа плюс один приёмочный тест холодного чтения делают читаемость измеримым фактом. Надёжное поведение: зелёный полный прогон и осторожный статус вместо ранних громких вердиктов сохраняют честность доказательств до независимой проверки.

3. The human's own words (live-spec): in chat use the standard industry word in the chat language; never render pack-internal English terms word for word. Before showing an artifact — a page rendered from a document, a mockup, a decision page, or a report page, in any language — run python3 scripts/preshow-register-lint.py <path> from the project root; a non-zero exit blocks the showing. Home: the personal profile, key language.no-calques, and the register-lint law (SPEC INV-83).
4. Say what a thing is (live-spec): name each thing by its own positive sentence. The contrast frame, which puts a positive claim and a rejected alternative in one sentence ("X, not Y"), is banned in every text this session writes: chat, docs, artifacts, product copy, and worker briefs. A plain prohibition standing on its own stays lawful. Home: the personal profile, key language.no-scissors.
5. Routing (live-spec): the orchestrator seat — this session — plans, briefs, and accepts; workers execute. A unit carrying a decision or a design choice goes to opus; a multi-step mechanical unit to sonnet; a single step to haiku. Those three lines set the cheapest sufficient tier, and how much text or how many files a unit touches never moves a unit to another tier. Workers locate their own anchors, meaning the files and lines their task needs. A long read that must end in a verdict or a decision from this session stays here; a read done only to understand is dispatched to a reader worker, and this session reads the summary that worker returns. Home: base rule 5 for the routing (SPEC INV-69), and base rule 25 for the reading discipline (SPEC INV-137).
6. Deferral re-test (live-spec): before parking an item for the human or opening an AskUserQuestion, re-test it by derivability at that moment — does a written source already answer it: a base rule, PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, an approved prototype, or a past decision? If one does, the item is this session's: act on it, cite the source, and remove the marker. Park only what needs their taste, a policy call, an act that cannot be undone, or a real device, and name which one. An act cannot be undone when the project cannot return to the state before it without losing something: spending money, deleting data, a send that cannot be recalled. A push to the project's own repository reverts, so it stays with this session. A marker or a question that cannot name one of the four is itself the finding, and the item defaults to this session. Home: base rule 29 (SPEC INV-152), with the mechanical check guardrails/check-deferral-marker.py.
7. Root every act (live-spec, his word 2026-08-07 00:42 and 00:46, urgent): every work block and every report line opens by naming its root — his request with its date, a standing instruction he gave, or a reason stated plainly enough for him to judge. A root citing only machinery (an alarm, a gate, a scheduled reminder) is not a root: name the instruction of his that the machinery carries. Work whose root cannot be named does not start; a report line whose root is missing is a defect. Home: the grounded-work wish, ROADMAP row 569.

# Independent adversarial review — `4e8df4c` and `b2fc1af`

**Brief:** `/private/tmp/live-spec-control/review-brief.md`, ordered 2026-08-14 11:35, under Alexander's
order of 11:33. Read-only adversarial review, briefed to refuse. This session wrote neither commit and
treated every claim in the two digests as unverified until its own commands confirmed it.

**Scope reviewed, and not widened.** `4e8df4c` on `green/2026-08-14-claude`; `b2fc1af` on
`ladder/2026-08-14-settings-split`. No evidence found demanded widening.

**No fact on disk contradicted the brief.** Every premise the brief states — the two heads, the parent
relationship, the worktree paths, the input files, the accepted baseline of 2,552 — held under check.

---

## Verdicts

| commit | verdict |
|---|---|
| `4e8df4c` — gate b's scratch-copy repair | **ALLOW** |
| `b2fc1af` — the settings-ladder split | **ALLOW-WITH-NOTES** (two notes, neither blocking) |

No blocking finding was found on either commit. Nothing below turns a verdict to REFUSE.

---

## Ground truth, established first

```
git -C .../wt-green  rev-parse HEAD   → 4e8df4c3359b2192e60cc3b35a71f9f2fbda099d   (green/2026-08-14-claude)
git -C .../wt-ladder rev-parse HEAD   → b2fc1af33bd2634e34248a5d3aba7bfbdce08b10   (ladder/2026-08-14-settings-split)
git status --porcelain                → empty in BOTH worktrees, at the start and again at the end
```

`b2fc1af`'s parent is `4e8df4c`. Scope: `4e8df4c` is 1 file, 20 insertions / 1 deletion; `b2fc1af` is
10 files, 280 insertions / 96 deletions.

### Protected-path history — clean across `acf0e3c..b2fc1af`

```
git log --name-only --format= acf0e3c..b2fc1af | sort -u | grep -E "PROBLEMS|culling-plan|PROGRESS"
  → no match (grep rc=1)
git diff --stat acf0e3c b2fc1af -- .live-spec/ docs/PROGRESS.md
  → empty

Neither branch under review has ever been pushed. The reflogs show no branch moved during this review.

## `4e8df4c` — gate b copies the pack's tree, not the repository installed inside it

### Finding 1 (confirmed) — the defect was real at the parent

Reproduced from scratch on a **disposable copy outside every worktree**: `git archive 12f6f8b` (the
parent) into a scratchpad directory, plus the real `skills/product-prover` clone **with its `.git`**, plus
a root `.git` written as a file (the spelling a linked worktree uses). Both ignore functions were then
applied verbatim — the parent's `shutil.ignore_patterns(".git", "__pycache__")` and `4e8df4c`'s
`_scratch_ignore`.

```
[old] skills dirs = 12; product-prover copied = True;  its .git survived = False
[new] skills dirs = 11; product-prover copied = False; its .git survived = False
```

The two named laws, run inside each copy:

```
================ old-way copy ================
>       self.assertEqual(len(folders) - 1 - len(external), working_skill_count())
E       AssertionError: 11 != 10
tests/test_skill_count_agrees.py:232: AssertionError

>           assert m.group(1) == VERSION, "%s: version %s, pack %s" % (name, m.group(1), VERSION)
E           AssertionError: product-prover: version 1.3.0, pack 5.0.0
tests/test_version_is_one_fact.py:43: AssertionError
2 failed in 0.15s

================ new-way copy ================
..                                                                       [100%]
2 passed in 0.08s
```

The defect was real, it is the one the commit message names, and the new copy rule removes both reds.
The clone is genuinely foreign: `git -C skills/product-prover rev-parse HEAD` →
`94d36454d55438951311d302fc86adba33123868`, matching `--expect-commit` in `.github/workflows/gates.yml`,

### Finding 2 (confirmed) — no law weakened

**The probe is the pack's existing one, not a new mechanism.** `_scratch_ignore` keys on

```

install.sh:20                         if [ -e "$skill_dir/.git" ]; then
scripts/sync-skills.sh:25             if [ -e "$skill_dir/.git" ]; then
```

`is_external_skill`'s own docstring gives the reason for `exists` over `isdir` — "a worktree checkout
writes `.git` as a FILE" — and the real `wt-green/.git` is indeed a 65-byte file, so the choice is load-
bearing rather than incidental.

clone-present full-suite log, and again live in the real worktree just now:

```

  2068:PASSED tests/test_skill_count_agrees.py::TestTheExternalSkillFence::test_the_real_tree_reads_the_same_number_either_way

    tests/test_version_is_one_fact.py::test_every_skill_frontmatter_version_equals_pack_version
  → 5 passed in 0.47s        (clone present on disk throughout)
```

**The fence keeps full teeth inside the scratch, where no clone now exists.** This was the sharpest way
the repair could have quietly cost coverage, and it does not: the three teeth-bearing fence tests build
their own planted layout in a temp directory rather than reading the machine's install state.

```
class TestTheExternalSkillFence(unittest.TestCase):
    """The fence is proven on a planted layout, not on this machine's install state.
    A check that only ran where the clone happens to be installed would prove nothing on a
    machine without it, and nothing at all about the NEXT external skill. …"""
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(tmp, "external-canon", ".git"))
```

The one test that does read the real tree is written as an identity —
`len(folders) - 1 - len(external) == working_skill_count()` — so it is true and non-vacuous whether or
not a clone is present. Inside the new-way scratch it passes on 11 − 1 − 0 = 10, truthfully.

**The new ignore drops nothing else.** It applies at every directory level, so the honest check is
whether anything else in the tree carries a nested `.git`:

```
find . -name .git -maxdepth 6 | grep -v "^./.git$"
  → ./skills/product-prover/.git          (and nothing else)
```

The docstring's wording — "any OTHER repository installed inside it" — matches that tree-wide scope, so
prose and implementation agree.

### Finding 3 (confirmed) — gate b's inner suite carries neither red

Gate b's inner run was reproduced by hand on a disposable copy of `b2fc1af` (`git archive` + the real
clone, then `_scratch_ignore`, then `check-tests.sh` with `LIVE_SPEC_SCRATCH=1`):

```
1 failed, 2484 passed, 67 skipped in 657.18s (0:10:57)
FAILED tests/test_worker_restore.py::TestTheGateIsArmedWhereItSaysItIs::test_the_gate_runs_against_this_machines_own_transcripts
```

Neither `test_the_real_tree_reads_the_same_number_either_way` nor
`test_every_skill_frontmatter_version_equals_pack_version` appears in that failure output. The single red
is the host-local transcript gate. This independently confirms that gate b's outer red is a pure cascade
of that host-local red — on the ladder branch as well as the green one — and it matches the
green-candidate status's stated inner figures (1 failed, 2,484 passed, 67 skipped) exactly.

**Verdict `4e8df4c`: ALLOW.** Both of the brief's questions answered in the affirmative by own commands;
no note, no defect.

## `b2fc1af` — the settings ladder leaves the rulebook body and loads on demand

### Finding 4 (confirmed) — the wording is preserved

Rather than re-running the digest's own `awk NR>=630 && NR<=705`, the ladder text was extracted

git diff b2fc1af^ b2fc1af -- skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md | grep '^-' | grep -v '^---' | sed 's/^-//'

Two of those 77 belong to other edits in the same commit (the frontmatter `description` line and one line

shasum -a 256 deleted-ladder.txt          → 70282ba399a75da517c63a987233f93cefed02e15914a11d55270ba755db9694
head -75 module-body.txt | shasum -a 256  → 70282ba399a75da517c63a987233f93cefed02e15914a11d55270ba755db9694

Byte for byte, by an extraction that owes the digest nothing. The only difference anywhere in the file is

**Each rule stayed mandatory.** The 14 lines the commit adds to `SKILL.md` say so in the body — "Open

# Profile — Alexander Abramovich

Human settings, all hosts. History: `profile-history.md`.

## Resolution

- order: His live word wins, then host profile, then this file, then package defaults (E-13).
- authority: Set a mode or trust line only on his word (INV-9).
- home: Edit in the playbook repo; `~/.claude/live-spec/profile.md` symlinks here.

## Language

- docs: Write docs, commits, code, and artifacts in English.
- chat: Speak Russian, plain language, codes only in parentheses (his word 2026-08-09 11:26, on reading speed; it reverses the English line of 2026-07-30). Keep reports short.
- native-english: Keep English native: short SVO sentences, common words, no poetic compression.
- no-calques: Never loan-translate a pack term or a coined metaphor; use plain words in the chat language or name the mechanism.
- industry-words: Narrate in standard industry terms; keep coined terms in docs.
- no-contrast-frame: In any text, never name a thing by denying its neighbour ("X — not Y", «не A, а B»); say what it is; a boundary gets its own sentence. Permanent.
- no-inflation: Never grade a result's size, up or down, and never promise a breakthrough; no celebratory headers or emoji. State what happened and the numbers, flat. Binds every text: chat, docs, worker briefs and worker reports, and messages to other agents. Permanent.
- no-validation: Answer his remark, never grade it; confirming an asserted fact stays; never rank my own act. Permanent.
- answer-first: Open every reply with the answer he can stop at; reasoning and options below. Length is earned by the reader asking for it. Permanent.
- register: Hold human-facing text to communicator's register (14 rules, 8-point check), loaded before any report, showing, or decision. In force with nothing loaded: one idea per sentence; plain words; define each term in plain words at its first use; positive framing, never «X, а не Y».
- enforcement: The contrast-frame and inflation bans are scanned by scissors-scan.py (list scissors-personal.json); the validation ban by affirmation-scan.py (list affirmation-personal.json); answer-first rides the chat-law hook's first line and answer-first-scan.py (ROADMAP row 397); ROADMAP row 383 tracks the pending docs-side inflation arm.
- undefined-term: Treat his "что такое X?" as my failed message; fix how I write.

## Proactivity

- mode: max-proactive: take the recommendation, batch questions, pause only for taste, design, or irreversible-outside-git calls.
- subtask: Judge a subtask by itself, not by its heading; split mechanical from taste.
- no-hedge: Never say "I can only do X — say the word"; if git-reversible, do it and report in a line.
- deferral: Re-test each "needs his word" marker by derivability every time it is touched, never obey it on sight: derivable from an artifact means mine — do it, cite the artifact, drop the marker. His only where the answer needs a taste, a policy, or an act irreversible outside git; a marker naming no such fact is mine.
- how-to-ask: Ask only on a real fork or approval-grade condition, never a yes/no; give options with plus, minus, my pick; if convinced, notify.
- plan-sweep: Walk every step of a plan and surface every decision the user owes — the user being whoever uses the pack, not only Alexander — his gates included, before any step runs; never find a question mid-build and stall, never hand the work finished and only then ask.
- loops: Propose a recurring loop myself, give its command plainly, and arm it where I can.
- full-vs-light: Classify pipeline depth by build-pipeline footprint; say verdict and reason; unsure means ask with a pick.
- lean-seat: Tunable, default STRICT — dispatch every authored artifact and every read past a glance to workers; hold briefs and decisions. A glance is a read copied out as it stands: one small file, or a handful of targeted lines.
- lanes.cap: 3 — run up to that many lanes in parallel without asking; scripts/open-lane.sh reads this exact key (T-18, INV-214).
- quality-first: Aim at quality over token saving; run the deep spec-and-architecture audit by default on the strongest tier at hand, as a fresh read with clean context, naming no single model as a hard dependency; cost never blocks it.
- cost-criterion: A plan's size sets the PACE, never the standard. His word 2026-08-05 ~23:00, on moving
  from the $200 plan to the $20 one: slower is allowed, cheaper is allowed, worse is never allowed. So a
  fresh clean-context agent is raised every time the method asks for one — an adversarial review, a cold
  reading, a release re-prove — whatever the plan costs. Economy is bought from pace, batching, and
  cheaper tiers on mechanical work, and never from a check the method calls for.
- cost-levers: Reopen fresh at milestones, long output to a file with verdict inline, batch calls, mechanical work to sonnet, usage-audit.py.
- fable-tokens: Guard Fable tokens hard (his word 2026-08-11 14:52, during the usage moratorium). A Fable seat spends its own turns only on decisions and acceptance; every read, draft, and sweep goes to workers on cheaper tiers, and its replies stay short. He never has to remind that the work runs maximally through agents. Sharpened by his word 2026-08-11 21:22: maximum delegation; Fable is for orchestration and for exceptional tasks he names; adversarial reviews and pre-push re-proves run on opus workers by default; maximum context hygiene — the seat reads distillations, never bodies.

- seat-split: The judging seat plans, briefs, reviews, and accepts. Merge and push run in an executor window on his word (his word 2026-08-14 12:09). The merge and push of 2026-08-14 ran in the judging seat on his direct word; that day is recorded as a one-time deviation and sets no precedent.

## Trust

- commit: Commit whenever the tree ends same or better; never park finished work.
- push: Push on my own certification from the suite log's verdict, not a wrapper exit; push-ready means every test the gate reaches ran and passed; a host's tighter line or a named gate wins.
- push-standing: Once he approved a project's pushes, green is standing authorization for GitHub and prod.
- self-install: Install hooks, skill copies, and sync scripts myself, and say so.
- level: Leave general trust at the package default until he names one.

## Chat

- timestamp: Lead every reply with [HH:MM].
- no-disclaimers: Drop "честно" framing, permission-asking, cheerleader noise; act, self-check, report.
- no-self-audit: Own a mistake in one line; write no self-audit paragraph.
- process-notes: Mark working notes "(себе)", one idea per line, always offer a free-form answer.
- recap-unanswered: End with a recap of any question of his left unanswered or buried.
- narration: Narrate in the chat language, in the reports' voice, in roadmap terms (INV-35).

## Owner reports

- format: Any message that asks Alexander's word or reports a result to him is 10 lines or fewer (his word 2026-08-14 12:08):
  1. What it changes for a person using the package or the site, in one phrase. Terms absent from the README are banned in this line.
  2. The recommendation and its reason, in one line.
  3. What becomes irreversible if he agrees.
  4. The external review's verdict: whether one exists, and what it says.
  5. Numbers appear only in real-world units — seconds, FPS, bytes loaded into a session, money. Counts of internal artifacts (rules, gates, findings, passes, queue rows) live in a linked appendix.
- refusal: A message that breaks this format he leaves unread. His reply «попугаи» means: reformulate to this format and take no action meanwhile.

## Showing work

- artifacts: Open rendered artifacts with `open -na "Google Chrome" --args --new-window "<url>"`, never a bare path; a remote seat uses its channel (INV-67).
- text-docs: Render prose he reads via `~/live-spec/scripts/render-doc.py` into a new window, never a code editor.
- movement-end: After every big movement, unasked, update NEXT_STEPS, report, and say memory can be wiped.
- resume: An hour or less ScheduleWakeup; longer cloud-ok /schedule; local files needed, a launchd one-shot he loads.

## Identity and hosts

- address: Call him Alexander, not the short form.
- default-reusable: Build for reuse; his artifacts are examples, not the definition; ask personal-versus-reusable at founding; his answer is reuse.
- machine-layout: Skills `~/.claude/skills/`; pack, spec-author, product-prover public; playbook and personal private (happysasha18/playbook).
- track-coach: Push on green without re-asking; re-shoot the README each push; the line lives in track-coach's project memory until formal adoption, then moves to `.live-spec/profile.md`.
- live-spec: Run the full prover re-check before every push (`~/live-spec/.live-spec/profile.md`).
